headline: Hot US Inflation And Federal Reserve Rate Hawks Trigger Massive Gold Slump
paragraphs: Crude oil rallied today, with Brent up 3.41 percent to EUR 86.71 and WTI up 2.38 percent to EUR 80.09, driven by geopolitical risks and reports of strikes involving Iran that offset rising crude output and Middle East settlement hopes. Natural gas jumped 4.17 percent on the day and 11.71 percent for the week to EUR 3.03, supported by ramping demand and colder US weather forecasts.

Gold plunged 2.10 percent today and 3.89 percent for the week down to EUR 3540.52, hitting a 13-month low as a hot CPI print lifted yields and aggressive Fed rate hawks crushed prices below the 4,000 dollar mark. Silver fell 2.50 percent to EUR 45.73 amid persistent downside momentum and Fed pressure. Palladium dropped 3.28 percent to EUR 912.59, while the causes for the daily moves in platinum, copper, and WTI crude are unclear from the available news.
The euro traded at 1.1062 against the US dollar, cushioning some import costs for Irish businesses.
